Chocolate Brownie Lava Cake 🍫🌋 Ingredients: - For Chocolate Sponge - • 240g plain flour • 30g cocoa powder • 400g granulated sugar • 2tsp bicarbonate of soda • 1tsp baking powder • 240ml milk • 110g vegetable oil • 2 large eggs • 1tsp vanilla extract • 50g milk chocolate • 150ml hot water - For Chocolate Icing - • 250g unsalted butter • 500g icing sugar • 50g cocoa powder • 1tsp vanilla extract • 3tbsp milk - For Brownie Lava - • 100g light brown sugar • 50g granulated sugar • 70g unsalted butter • 40g cocoa powder • 40g plain flour (heat treated) • 80g double cream • 1tsp vanilla extract • a pinch of salt • 70g milk chocolate - For Brownie Bites - • 100g light brown sugar • 50g granulated sugar • 90g unsalted butter • 60g cocoa powder • 120g plain flour (heat treated) • 2-3tbsp double cream • 1tsp vanilla extract • a pinch of salt • 100g chocolate chips Instructions: - For Chocolate Sponge - 1) In a large bowl, combine your flour, cocoa powder, granulated sugar, bicarbonate of soda, and baking powder 2) In another bowl, whisk together your milk, vegetable oil, eggs, vanilla extract, and 50g melted milk chocolate 3) Fold in your dry ingredients from before and add in 150ml hot water or coffee 4) Line three 8” cake tins and pour in the batter evenly. Bake in the oven at 160°C fan for around 25 minutes - For Icing - 1) Whisk your butter until light and creamy 2) Add in your icing sugar and cocoa powder 3) Once incorporated, whisk in your vanilla and milk until fluffy  - For Brownie Lava - 1) Melt the butter with both sugars over a medium heat 2) Whisk in the cocoa powder and flour 3) Gradually add in the cream until molten and thick, then stir in the vanilla extract and salt 4) Let it cool to just above room temperature and then add in the milk chocolate to slowly melt in 5) Once the lava has reached room temperature, you can use it on your cake! - For Bronwie Bites - 1) Cream together the butter and both sugars until fluffy 2) Mix in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt until sandy 3) Add in the vanilla extract and double cream 4) Once it has become a dough, fold in your chocolate chips, then press it firmly into a lined 9x9” square tin, refrigerate for 30 minutes, then cut into small bite sized pieces  Watch the video to see how I build and decorate the cake! I find it’s easier to ice the sponges when they are frozen/cold. Enjoy! :) #chocolate #cake #brownie #baking #recipes

Coca-Cola Cake 🥤🍫 This old-fashioned Coca-Cola Cake is rich, incredibly moist, and covered with a warm chocolate frosting that melts right into the cake. Mini marshmallows bake into the batter, giving this nostalgic 9×13 cake an extra-soft texture. You can get the more detailed version with extra tips, step-by-step help, and a printable recipe on my website. Visit my blog through the link in my bio! For the cake: 2 cups all-purpose flour 2 cups granulated sugar ½ teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon baking soda 1 cup Coca-Cola 1 cup salted butter ⅓ cup unsweetened cocoa powder ½ cup buttermilk 2 large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 cup mini marshmallows For the frosting: ½ cup salted butter 3 Tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder 6 Tablespoons Coca-Cola 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 3¾ cups powdered sugar 1 cup chopped pecans or walnuts, optional Instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9×13-inch baking dish. Whisk together the flour, sugar, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl. In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the Coca-Cola, butter, and cocoa powder. Heat until the butter melts and the mixture just begins to simmer, whisking occasionally. Pour the hot cocoa mixture into the dry ingredients and whisk until combined. Add the buttermilk, eggs, and vanilla, stirring just until smooth. Fold in the mini marshmallows. Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and bake for 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs. About five minutes before the cake finishes baking, melt the butter with the cocoa powder and Coca-Cola in a saucepan over medium heat. Remove it from the heat and whisk in the vanilla and powdered sugar until smooth. Stir in the nuts, if using. Pour the warm frosting over the warm cake and spread it evenly. Let the frosting set before slicing. #cocacolacake #chocolatecake #southerndessert #oldfashionedrecipes #cakerecipe Coca-Cola cake recipe, old-fashioned Coca-Cola cake, Southern chocolate cake, chocolate sheet cake, 9×13 cake recipe, chocolate cake with warm frosting, nostalgic dessert recipe

Halloween Spider Lava Cakes  Ingredients - 15g all-purpose flour made from U.S. wheat - 170g dark couverture chocolate - 110g unsalted butter - A pinch of salt - 3 large eggs, at room temperature - ½ tsp vanilla extract - 50g granulated sugar - Marshmallows, for decorating - Candy or chocolate eyes, optional Instructions 1. Preheat the oven to 200°C. 2. Lightly grease oven-safe ramekins with butter. Dust the insides with a thin layer of cocoa powder, then tap out any excess.  3. In a heatproof bowl, combine the dark couverture chocolate, butter, and salt. Microwave for 1 minute, stir until smooth and evenly combined then set aside. 4. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, vanilla extract, and granulated sugar until pale, slightly thickened, and fluffy. 5. Pour the warm chocolate mixture into the egg mixture. Gently whisk until evenly combined. 6. Add the flour and mix until just combined. Do not overmix. 7. Divide the batter evenly among the prepared ramekins, filling each approximately three-quarters full. 8. Bake at 200°C for 8–9 minutes, or until the edges are set but the centres remain soft. The precise baking time will depend on the size and material of the ramekins. 9. Allow the cakes to rest for 1–2 minutes. Carefully loosen the edges with a knife, then invert each cake onto a serving plate. 10. Place the marshmallows in a microwave-safe bowl and microwave for 1 minute, or until softened and melted. Stir briefly to combine, then allow to cool for about 5 minutes. 11. Take a small amount of melted marshmallow between your fingers, stretch it into thin strands, and gently drape it over the lava cakes to create a spiderweb effect. 12. Add candy or chocolate eyes for a fun, spider-inspired finish. 13. Serve immediately while the centres are still warm and molten. Le secret du Gâteau Volcan : Moelleux et irrésistible ! 🌋🍫. 1.La base : Battre les œufs avec le sucre et la vanille jusqu’à ce que le mélange blanchisse. 2.Les liquides : Ajouter l’huile tout en continuant de battre, puis verser le lait. 3.Le secret de la texture : Incorporer la farine (environ 300g) petit à petit. Attention : la quantité peut varier selon la qualité de votre farine (certaines absorbent plus que d’autres !). 4.La touche finale : Ajouter le cacao et la levure chimique en même temps que la farine. 5.	Le montage : Verser la pâte dans un moule de 27 cm de diamètre, puis déposer délicatement au centre la crème pâtissière maison. 6.	La cuisson : Enfourner à 180°C pendant 40 minutes. Allumer uniquement le bas au début, puis le haut en fin de cuisson pour dorer. 7.	La déco : Une touche de zeste de citron et du chocolat râpé pour le contraste des saveurs. 🍋🍫 Bon appétit ! ❤️ #GâteauVolcan #CakeChocolat #PatisserieMaison #RecetteFacile

BRIGADEIRO VOLCANO CAKE 🥕🐇🍫 This is a classic Brigadeiro Carrot Cake I grew up eating: super soft, moist, and topped with warm brigadeiro  Recipe Cake 400g carrots, peeled and chopped 6 eggs 2½ cups sugar 1½ cups neutral oil 4 cups all-purpose flour (sifted) 2 tbsp baking powder 1 pinch salt Preheat oven to 340°F / 170°C and grease a 15-cup bundt pan well. Blend the carrots and oil for about 1 minute, add the eggs and sugar and blend 2-3 minutes until completely smooth. In a bowl, sift the flour, pour in the carrot mixture and mix gently just until combined. Add a pinch of salt and the baking powder last and mix lightly. Pour into the pan, tap it a couple times on the counter to release air bubbles, and bake 50-60 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Let cool 10-15 minutes before removing from the pan. Brigadeiro Topping 2 cans sweetened condensed milk 4 tbsp cocoa powder 1 tbsp butter 7 oz / 200 g heavy cream Cook the condensed milk, cocoa, and butter over medium-low heat, stirring constantly until slightly thickened. Turn off the heat and stir in the heavy cream to make it silky and pourable. TIP: mix the cocoa powder with a bit of heavy cream first before adding to the condensed milk mixture While it's still warm, pour it over the center of the cake and let it overtlow.

Chocolate Volcano Cake Ingredients: 200g dark chocolate (70%) 150g butter 150g sugar 3 eggs 100g flour 25g cocoa powder 8g vanilla sugar 2g salt 3-4g baking powder (optional, for a fluffier texture) Preparation: Melting Chocolate and Butter Break the chocolate into pieces, mix it with butter, and melt over a double boiler or in the microwave (in short 20-second intervals, stirring in between). Making the Batter In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs with sugar and vanilla sugar until light and fluffy. Pour in the melted chocolate and butter mixture, then stir well. Sift in the flour, cocoa powder, salt, and baking powder (if using). Mix gently. Baking Preheat the oven to 170°C. Pour the batter into a 20cm round cake tin lined with parchment paper. Bake for 20-25 minutes. The cake should remain slightly moist inside (check with a toothpick—it should come out slightly sticky). Cooling and Serving Let the cake cool completely in the tin. Optionally, dust with powdered sugar or serve with a scoop of ice cream and caramel. Enjoy! 🍫🎂 #cake #easyrecipe #cupcakes #foodlover #brownies #chocolate #dessert #foodtok #fyp #cookie
